title: FastQC warnings after mixing NovaSeq lanes in one CASSIE job
body: I merged reads from two NovaSeq lanes before uploading to Storage, then ran FastQC in CASSIE. The per-tile quality warning appears in only one lane, but the combined report makes it look sample-wide. Would you split lanes into separate tool blocks or keep one FastQC job for the sample?
author: Aylin

comments.author: Mert
comments.body: @Aylin I would run FastQC per lane first, then create a second job on the merged reads only after checking whether the warning is localized.

comments.author: Priya
comments.body: If the same sample has consistent adapter and GC profiles, the merge is fine for downstream assembly. The lane-level FastQC job is mostly for diagnosing the instrument artifact.

comments.author: Jon
comments.body: @Mert agreed. In CASSIE, I name the lane jobs with lane IDs so the Jobs page stays searchable later.

comments.author: Deniz
comments.body: Choose the VM based on how many FastQC files you are batching. You cannot set memory manually per job, so a larger VM profile is the knob if the batch is heavy.

title: SPAdes pipeline input mapping for paired-end reads
body: I built a saved pipeline with FastQC followed by SPAdes. In Create Job, CASSIE exposes the FASTQ input block and lets me map multiple files. For paired-end bacterial reads, should I map both R1 and R2 files into the same block or create separate inputs in the pipeline builder?
author: Burak

comments.author: Elif
comments.body: @Burak Map both R1 and R2 to the same FASTQ input block if the requirement accepts multiple FASTQ files. Keep filenames clear so SPAdes pairing can be inferred.

comments.author: Hannah
comments.body: I usually upload `sample_R1.fastq.gz` and `sample_R2.fastq.gz` together in Storage, then select both in the same pipeline input step.

comments.author: Ozan
comments.body: @Elif If you have multiple samples, create separate jobs rather than putting all samples into one SPAdes run.

title: QUAST comparison for assemblies created from manual tools vs saved pipeline
body: I ran SPAdes and QUAST manually, then repeated the same tools from a saved CASSIE pipeline. QUAST metrics matched, but the job history is easier to read from the saved pipeline. Is there any reason to prefer one route for reproducibility?
author: Nora

comments.author: Lara
comments.body: Saved pipelines are better for team reuse because the graph records the intended order. Manual tool selection is fine for quick experiments.

comments.author: Kerem
comments.body: @Nora I would use saved pipelines for anything you expect to rerun. The input mapping and VM choice are easier to audit.

comments.author: Sam
comments.body: For exact reproducibility, also keep the same uploaded input files and the same VM profile. CASSIE users choose VM profiles, not custom RAM values.

comments.author: Nina
comments.body: @Sam Good point. I include the VM name in my lab notes with the QUAST report.

title: BUSCO lineage choice for fungal assemblies
body: I have a draft fungal assembly from long reads and want to run BUSCO in CASSIE. The species is poorly annotated, so I am unsure whether to use a broad fungi lineage or a narrower lineage from a related clade. What do people do first?
author: Cem

comments.author: Irem
comments.body: @Cem Start broad if taxonomy is uncertain, then rerun with the narrower lineage once you confirm the placement.

comments.author: Marco
comments.body: A narrower lineage can inflate missing BUSCOs if the organism is outside the expected clade. I compare both and report the lineage name explicitly.

comments.author: Selin
comments.body: Use a larger VM profile if the assembly is big or if the lineage data is heavy. There is no per-job memory slider in CASSIE.

title: GenomeScope2 estimate looks off for heterozygous plant data
body: GenomeScope2 in my CASSIE workflow predicts a genome size about 20 percent lower than our flow cytometry estimate. The k-mer histogram has a wide heterozygous peak and a long tail. Could read contamination be driving this?
author: Leyla

comments.author: Arda
comments.body: @Leyla Contamination can do that, but high heterozygosity and repeats can also distort the model. I would run a k-mer spectrum after trimming and filtering.

comments.author: Mina
comments.body: Check whether organelle reads are overrepresented. They can add a strange tail and make interpretation harder.

comments.author: Emre
comments.body: I like to pair GenomeScope2 with Merqury later, especially if you have a draft assembly to compare against the read set.

comments.author: Aylin
comments.body: @Emre Same. The CASSIE job notes make it easy to keep those estimates beside the assembly evaluation jobs.

title: Choosing VM profiles for hifiasm jobs in CASSIE
body: We are assembling a 900 Mb genome with PacBio HiFi reads using hifiasm. Since CASSIE only lets us choose a VM profile and not manually allocate memory, what signals should we use to pick the VM before submitting?
author: Deniz

comments.author: Nina
comments.body: @Deniz Look at genome size, read coverage, and whether the sample is highly heterozygous. For hifiasm, I would avoid the smallest VM profile for 900 Mb.

comments.author: Kerem
comments.body: The runtime prediction is useful for cost planning, but for failed-memory risk I still choose the larger VM profile when coverage is high.

comments.author: Priya
comments.body: Exactly. In CASSIE the VM profile controls the available resource slice; users do not enter custom memory or CPU limits.

comments.author: Jon
comments.body: @Priya This is also easier for shared clusters because everyone uses the same configured profiles.

title: Verkko pipeline with HiFi plus ONT reads
body: I am setting up a saved CASSIE pipeline for Verkko using HiFi reads and ONT reads. Should I keep separate FASTQ input blocks for the two read technologies, or upload all reads into one block and document the distinction in filenames?
author: Sam

comments.author: Lara
comments.body: @Sam Separate input blocks are cleaner because the technologies have different roles in Verkko.

comments.author: Burak
comments.body: I name the blocks `HiFi reads` and `ONT reads` in the Create Job input step. It prevents mistakes when another lab member reruns the pipeline.

comments.author: Mert
comments.body: If the saved pipeline already has clear blocks, the final review page is much easier to inspect before submission.

title: Merqury k-mer completeness after polishing
body: After polishing a long-read assembly, Merqury reports improved QV but slightly lower k-mer completeness. The input reads are the same. Has anyone seen this after removing duplicate haplotigs?
author: Zeynep

comments.author: Marco
comments.body: @Zeynep Yes, purging duplicated haplotigs can reduce apparent completeness if true heterozygous sequence was removed.

comments.author: Irem
comments.body: Compare spectra-cn plots before and after purging. The QV alone will not tell the whole story.

comments.author: Elif
comments.body: In CASSIE, I keep separate Merqury jobs for pre-polish, post-polish, and post-purge assemblies so the results are not mixed.

comments.author: Ozan
comments.body: @Elif Same pattern here. The job names matter a lot when several assemblies are moving through the same project.

title: Liftoff transfer from reference annotation to alternate assembly
body: I am using Liftoff in CASSIE to transfer annotations from a close reference to a newly assembled cultivar. Several disease-resistance gene clusters are fragmented. Should I rerun with relaxed identity settings or inspect the assembly first?
author: Mina

comments.author: Cem
comments.body: @Mina Inspect the assembly around those clusters first. Resistance loci can be copy-rich and structurally variable.

comments.author: Hannah
comments.body: Relaxing identity helps sometimes, but it can also create questionable mappings. I would check QUAST and BUSCO around the same assembly version.

comments.author: Arda
comments.body: If you rerun, keep the same VM profile and change only the Liftoff flags. That makes the result comparison easier.

title: Metagenome assembly: metaSPAdes then QUAST or bin first?
body: For a complex wastewater metagenome, I ran metaSPAdes in CASSIE and got a fragmented assembly. Is it more useful to run QUAST on the whole assembly first, or should I bin contigs and evaluate bins separately?
author: Ozan

comments.author: Nora
comments.body: @Ozan I run QUAST on the whole assembly first for a quick sanity check, then evaluate bins separately if binning is part of the analysis.

comments.author: Jon
comments.body: For wastewater, fragmentation is expected. Total assembled bases, contig length distribution, and mapping rate may be more informative than N50 alone.

comments.author: Priya
comments.body: Choose a VM profile with enough room for metaSPAdes upfront. CASSIE does not expose manual memory allocation during submission.

comments.author: Lara
comments.body: @Priya Also watch temporary storage. Large metagenomes can be more storage-bound than people expect.

title: Using CASSIE runtime predictions for grant budgeting
body: Our group wants to estimate compute cost for a batch of genome assemblies. The runtime prediction in Create Job gives price and balance hold for one job. How are people using this for planning a batch of 40 samples?
author: Levent

comments.author: Selin
comments.body: @Levent I estimate one representative sample per read-depth group, then multiply by the number of samples in that group.

comments.author: Deniz
comments.body: Do not mix tiny bacterial samples and large eukaryotic samples in one average. The tool breakdown in the prediction makes the difference obvious.

comments.author: Mert
comments.body: For CASSIE, budget by VM profile too. A larger VM can finish sooner but may have a different per-minute price.

comments.author: Aylin
comments.body: @Mert And remember the hold is not necessarily the final charge. The final charge tracks actual runtime within the configured cap.

title: Pipeline priority sets for independent QC tools
body: I have a saved CASSIE pipeline where FastQC and GenomeScope2 can both run before assembly. The priority sets page lets me choose order within the same level. Is there any downside to leaving both in default scheduler order?
author: Emre

comments.author: Kerem
comments.body: @Emre Default scheduler order is fine unless you need one result first for a review checkpoint.

comments.author: Nina
comments.body: I prioritize FastQC when I want a quick fail-fast signal before spending time on heavier downstream jobs.

comments.author: Burak
comments.body: The priority sets do not change memory allocation. They only influence order for runnable same-level tools.

title: Storage file naming conventions for reusable pipelines
body: We share saved CASSIE pipelines across three projects. The biggest source of mistakes is choosing the wrong FASTQ or FASTA file in the input mapping step. What naming convention has worked best for you?
author: Hannah

comments.author: Elif
comments.body: @Hannah We use `project_sample_platform_readtype_date` and keep R1/R2 at the end, like `oak_A12_illumina_R1_2026.fastq.gz`.

comments.author: Marco
comments.body: For assemblies, include version tags: `sample_hifiasm_v1.fa`, `sample_hifiasm_purged_v2.fa`, and so on.

comments.author: Irem
comments.body: I also rename input blocks in Create Job to match the expected role, such as `HiFi reads`, `ONT reads`, or `reference annotation`.

comments.author: Sam
comments.body: @Irem That saves a lot of confusion during final review, especially when a saved pipeline has several explicit inputs.

title: CAT annotation workflow after Liftoff
body: I am comparing CAT and Liftoff annotations for a mammalian assembly. Liftoff is fast and reference-guided, while CAT is heavier but gives a richer annotation workflow. Has anyone chained these in CASSIE for comparison?
author: Jon

comments.author: Zeynep
comments.body: @Jon I run them as separate branches from the same assembly input, then compare gene counts and missing orthologs afterward.

comments.author: Lara
comments.body: CAT can be more demanding, so select a VM profile that matches the size of the annotation job. You still do not set memory manually in CASSIE.

comments.author: Cem
comments.body: For publication, I would keep both outputs and document the evidence sources. They answer slightly different annotation questions.
